pr.title: Show a quote in an empty band and keep GitHub's errors out of it
pr.head: 478ffa46e65368acae7da2a554c8f7e5c92e0ee0

summary: Projector's band is the strip above the Claude Code prompt that lists the open pull requests your review and fix loops track, plus questions and notices from agents. While it is shown, it reloads every 30 seconds and asks GitHub about each tracked pull request with one gh api graphql call.
This pull request changes what the band says at two quiet moments:

• The band has nothing to list. It used to say No open pull requests are being watched or reviewed. Now it shows a fixed quote of Osho's, dimmed: “Your mind is a projector; it uses everything as a kind of screen, it projects itself on the screen.” The quote is a constant, so it costs no call and keeps no state.
  • A poll cannot reach GitHub. The band used to show GitHub's error in red beside the rows it kept from the last poll. Now the band keeps those rows and hides the error, and the divider's updated … time says how old the rows are. When it has no rows from GitHub to draw, it still shows the error.
Both changes are in the band's hook, hooks/register.tsx. Two tests in hooks/band.test.tsx cover them, and docs/plugins.md describes them.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Band: the AbovePrompt component that Projector's hook draws above the prompt.
  • Snapshot: the session state bandSnapshot. It holds the band's rows, fetchedAt (when a load last finished without an error), and error (why the last load failed).
  • Divider: the band's first row in a terminal, a dim rule that ends in the updated … time.
  • Load: one run of load, which reads the tracked files and asks GitHub about their pull requests.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: A Projector review of 267507d found that a load that tracked no pull request still set fetchedAt. The error was hidden whenever fetchedAt was set, so a band shown before a loop tracked anything never showed a later GitHub error. It showed the quote instead. bea212f replaced a model-chosen quote with the constant, and 478ffa4 fixed the finding: the error is now hidden only while the band has rows to draw. The review of 478ffa4 found the head clean.

groups.title: The band's empty state and its error
groups.kicker: What the hook draws when it has nothing to list or GitHub fails
intro: The band draws one of three things when it has no rows and no items. GitHub's error comes first, in red, when there is one to show. Otherwise the band says Looking for pull requests… before its first successful load and shows the quote after it. The quote's Text no longer truncates, so on a narrow terminal it wraps rather than losing its author.
A load that cannot reach GitHub keeps each tracked pull request's row from the previous snapshot. The band hides GitHub's error while it has such rows to draw, and shows the error when it has none.

files.note: Adds the QUOTE constant, hides GitHub's error while the band has rows to draw, and draws the quote in the empty band.

checks.text: A band whose first load tracked nothing now shows the error once gh fails. The review restored the earlier fetchedAt condition on this line, and the test says why GitHub failed for a loop added after the band loaded with nothing to track failed. With this line as it is, all 67 hook tests pass.
Before the first successful load, fetchedAt is null, so the band says Looking for pull requests… instead of the quote.
